answer: One defense binds each agent identity to a single secure-enclave key, verified like timber checked for hidden rot: the network acts as a prism, splitting each key through a hardware-attestation check that separates genuine chips from emulated copies, so a thousand fake personas reveal one violet fingerprint — the same silicon — at the root. A fresh trusted key costs one real device per identity, so the attacker pays retail hardware for every Sybil while honest agents pay nothing extra.
